message.content: {"answer": "A", "option_text": "Presence of mediastinal air without adjacent lung opacification.", "reason": "Spontaneous pneumomediastinum (Hamman syndrome) results from alveolar rupture tracking along bronchovascular sheaths; radiographically, this presents as mediastinal air with clear lungs and absence of pleural effusion or consolidation. In contrast, esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome) typically causes chemical mediastinitis leading to adjacent lung opacification, pleural effusion, or hydropneumothorax. Option A correctly identifies the lack of parenchymal/pleural pathology as the discriminator favoring alveolar origin over esophageal perforation."}
